dossier.architecture: Dual-collector cargo cycling robot; onseason high-bar and offseason traversal configurations must be distinguished.

subsystems.drivetrain: Swerve-family architecture; exact module specification not established in this review.
subsystems.intake: Single collector at week 1; later opposed wide mecanum collectors supported drive-by pickup.
subsystems.transfer: Single-sided belts select upward storage or wrong-color passthrough.
subsystems.scoring: Range launcher; reviewed source establishes moving-shot virtual targeting added between second regional and Worlds. Exact hood/turret geometry remains unresolved.
subsystems.endgame: Onseason high-bar: an extension-envelope oversight compromised traversal. Reorientation before Worlds did not produce a sufficiently reliable fast traversal. Offseason added belted traversal, static hooks and pneumatic pivot.
subsystems.controls: Two-button driver workflow; opponent-cargo-only mode was implemented but reportedly never used.

versions: Onseason: dual intake and moving-shot software added.
Chezy interview shows a later traversal system, not the original Worlds climb.
dossier.analysis: The most useful lesson is the opportunity cost of endgame: a predictable high climb can outperform an unreliable traversal when alliance partners already cover the higher bars. Do not transfer the offseason climb into the Worlds performance explanation.
limits: Only the reviewed published configurations are established; intermediate changes may be undocumented.

context_documents.title: 2022-5940 · Dual acquisition improves route flexibility without proving every component optimal
context_documents.body:
# 2022-5940: Dual acquisition improves route flexibility without proving every component optimal

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

A second opposed collector was added after the single-intake early robot to support drive-by autonomous pickup. The source reports wide mecanum collectors, a controlled upward/passthrough belt path and a later moving-shot solution. The onseason climb differs from an offseason traversal upgrade.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team explicitly ties dual pickup to easier drive-by autonomous, while cautioning that its mecanum implementation required many iterations and was not a blanket recommendation.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

A successful robot can contain a mechanism the team would not copy again. Preserve that negative experience. Additional pickup directions buy route freedom, but require two transport-entry cases and greater repair exposure.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Compare complete auto routes, feed/rejection recovery and the exact onseason climb; do not back-project the offseason improvement.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.
